- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days after spike.  
- If model forecast is > 20% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until forecast aligns with recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; force a downward correction of 1–3% on next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; use 14-day moving average of true prices as a smoother baseline for correction.
